scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user provided a detailed scenario where a parent called the police on their daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing. The daughter was in sixth grade, and the parent noticed some extra money missing. They planted a $20 bill, and when the daughter took it, they called the police. The officers came to the school, and during this incident, the daughter revealed that there was a bully stealing her lunch money and she was also buying lunch for a friend who couldn't afford it. The parent's wife was upset, thinking this approach would damage their relationship with their daughter.

First, I need to understand the key points here. The parent's intention was to teach their daughter a lesson about stealing. They set up a situation where they could catch her in the act, then involved the police. However, it turned out that the daughter wasn't stealing; she was being bullied and helping a friend. The parent's action led to the daughter feeling scared and possibly losing a friend because of the attention brought to her financial situation.

Now, I should consider the moral aspects. The parent's intention was to correct a behavior they perceived as wrong. However, they didn't take the time to understand why the daughter was taking the money. Instead, they assumed it was stealing and took a harsh approach by involving the police. This led to a stressful situation for the daughter, who was actually dealing with bullying and trying to help a friend.

I think about the concept of punishment versus understanding. Punishing without understanding the underlying reasons can be counterproductive. It can lead to fear and mistrust, especially in a child. The parent's action might have made the daughter feel unsupported, especially since she was dealing with a bully and trying to help a friend.

Also, involving the police in a situation that turned out to be a misunderstanding could have long-term consequences. The daughter might feel that her parents don't trust her or that they are quick to involve authorities without considering her feelings or the context of her actions.

On the other hand, the parent was trying to teach a lesson about the consequences of stealing. However, the way they went about it was extreme and didn't consider the possibility that their daughter might be facing other issues. It's important to communicate and understand before taking such actions.

In conclusion, while the parent's intention was to teach a lesson, the method they used was harsh and didn't take into account the daughter's actual circumstances. This approach could damage the trust and relationship between the parent and child, and it might have been more effective to address the issue through communication and understanding rather than involving the police.
